targets.authors: Karmarkar, U. R., & Tormala, Z. L.
targets.title: Believe me, I have no idea what I’m talking about: The effects of source certainty on consumer involvement and persuasion.
targets.evidence_quote:
In this Registered Report, we conducted a highpowered (N = 1018) direct replication of Experiment 2 by Karmarkar and Tormala (2010). As an
exploratory test of the same mechanism, we included the two questions
measuring expectancy violation that were used by Karmarkar and Tor­
mala in Experiment 1.
targets.outcome_quote:
Overall, we must
conclude that our study failed to replicate the findings in the original,
and that we find support for the confidence heuristic hypothesis (H1b)
rather than the incongruity hypothesis (H1a).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly give an overall failure verdict; similarity for involvement does not override it. Experiment 2 is the primary target, with the expectancy-violation result of Experiment 1 also explicitly tested.

reasoning: Full published article matches title, DOI, four authors, and includes references. Completed Stage 2 registered report with newly collected Prolific data. Competing theories and sources of added measures are not separate targets.
